## Summary
- Add `finalize_policy: "defer"` support for delegated sub-orchestrator child work.
- Preserve immediate per-PR self-approval by default, but stop after `SHIP` and report readiness to the parent for trusted deferred child PRs.
- Update orchestrator guidance and regression coverage for immediate and deferred paths.

- `node --test dist/__tests__/handoff.test.js dist/__tests__/sub-orchestration.test.js dist/__tests__/orchestrate-handoff-cli.test.js`
- `git diff --check`

Closes #259

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 6c10bd6629ccbcb020895d59b99b55913b22e8cb -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #260 implements #259, which came from discussion #257 about preventing batch or stacked child PRs from self-approving and self-merging too early.
- The PR adds `finalize_policy: "defer"` metadata for sub-orchestrator children, stops trusted deferred child PRs after a `SHIP` review, and reports readiness back to the parent orchestrator.
- The intended product behavior is to preserve immediate per-PR self-approval for independent work while letting the parent finalize batch/stacked PRs later in dependency order.
- The implementation covers the deferral stop path, but the parent finalization and reuse behavior are not complete enough to ship as-is.

## Review
The reviewers agree the marker-based approach is small and fits the existing orchestration design. The main disagreement is severity: one review treated parent finalization as prompt-level guidance, but after checking #257 and runtime policy, the deferred flow currently has no automated way to finish.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Parent finalization has no dispatch path | BLOCKING | Deferred child PRs report “ready” to the parent, but the resumed issue-level parent orchestrator cannot dispatch `agent-self-approve` or `agent-self-merge` for that PR. |
| Reused child issues can ignore deferral | BLOCKING | `finalize_policy: "defer"` is applied to new or newly adopted children, but recorded, searched, or already-marked reusable children keep their existing marker policy. |
| Agent docs omit deferred finalization behavior | WARNING | `.agent/docs` still describes child orchestration as always following the normal self-approval/self-merge chain, which is stale for this behavior change. |

## Progress
- Implemented pieces include marker parsing/formatting, deferred `SHIP` stop behavior, parent progress reporting, prompt guidance, and focused tests for the main deferred path.
- The rubrics review passed overall and raised only INFO-level validation concerns for unknown `finalize_policy` values.
- Existing PR discussion had no inline review comments or review threads before synthesis.
- Posted two new inline comments: `.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md:103` and `.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts:810`.
- No comments were minimized, no replies were added, and no threads were resolved.
- Optional reviewer nits not elevated to required action items: unreachable validation guard, extra CLI assertion coverage, and stricter invalid-policy handling.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Parent finalization has no dispatch path</summary>

**Cause:** The prompt says deferred child PRs should be finalized by the parent later, but `reportTerminalToParent` resumes the parent as issue-level `orchestrate`, and `decideAgentHandoff` only allows issue-level orchestrate to dispatch `implement` or `delegate_issue`. PR-level orchestrate is also limited to `review` or `fix-pr`, so there is no runtime-supported parent path to self-approve the ready child PR.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a trusted parent finalization path that can dispatch `agent-self-approve` for ready deferred child PRs while preserving requester authorization and ordering constraints, or change the prompt/status/docs to state that finalization is manual.

**Comments:** Reviewer disagreement was material here. The originating discussion explicitly proposed that the parent dispatch final self-approval/self-merge after all child work is done, so this is treated as blocking rather than documentation-only.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reused child issues can ignore deferral</summary>

**Cause:** `ensureSubOrchestrationIssue` normalizes the requested finalize policy, but reuse paths for explicit trusted children, recorded children, and searched reusable children only update `parent_round`. If an existing marker is still immediate, a new planner decision with `finalize_policy: "defer"` can be ignored and the child PR can still self-approve on `SHIP`.

**Candidate solutions:** Reconcile the trusted marker policy during reuse, or reject conflicting reuse with a visible stop. Add regression coverage for explicit, recorded, and searched child reuse with a changed finalization policy.

**Comments:** This was posted inline at `.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts:810`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Agent docs omit deferred finalization behavior</summary>

**Cause:** The technical docs still say child issues follow the normal bounded chain including `agent-self-approve` and `agent-self-merge`, without documenting immediate vs deferred finalization.

**Candidate solutions:** Update `.agent/docs/technical-details/agent-orchestrator.md` and any short user-facing action docs that describe child orchestration/self-approval behavior.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR

Unresolved findings require concrete branch changes and are safe for an automated fix-pr pass scoped to orchestration policy, marker reconciliation, tests, and docs.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Add a runtime-supported parent finalization path for deferred ready child PRs, preserving requester authorization and dependency order.
- [ ] Reconcile or reject `finalize_policy` changes when reusing existing trusted child issues, with regression coverage.
- [ ] Update `.agent/docs` to describe immediate vs deferred sub-orchestrator finalization behavior.

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 37c32e2a5f179b695d336e9e7de8d0dc0ece343b -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #260 implements #259 from discussion #257 by adding deferred finalization for batch or stacked child PRs.
- Independent child PRs keep the existing per-PR `SHIP -> agent-self-approve -> agent-self-merge` behavior.
- Deferred child PRs stop after `SHIP`, report readiness to the parent, and the parent can later dispatch self-approval in dependency order.
- A prior fix-pr pass addressed earlier blockers around parent finalization dispatch, child reuse policy reconciliation, and docs.

## Review
The current head fixes the earlier synthesis blockers, but one retry path can still leave a deferred child PR ready and unfinalized. Reviewers otherwise agree the design is small and aligned with existing orchestration patterns; the main disagreement is that the stale Claude review was against the pre-fix commit and did not cover the new retry edge.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Deferred finalization retry can stall | BLOCKING | If parent-dispatched self-approval returns `REQUEST_CHANGES`, the later `fix-pr -> review -> SHIP` path is suppressed as deferred readiness again and does not resume parent finalization. |
| Non-blocking cleanup/test coverage nits remain | INFO | A stale reviewer noted an unreachable finalize-policy guard and a missing direct CLI assertion for created child issue body propagation; these are minor and not required action items. |

## Progress
- Earlier blockers are addressed: parent `agent-self-approve` dispatch exists, reused child issues reconcile `finalize_policy`, and `.agent/docs` describe deferred finalization.
- Posted one new inline comment at `.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts:1100`.
- Resolved two older same-agent threads after verifying authorship and fixes: `.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md:108` and `.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts:929`.
- No replies were added and no comments were minimized.
- The synthesis did not rerun tests; reviewer notes report prior build/test checks, and the remaining blocker comes from tracing current head behavior.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Deferred finalization retry can stall</summary>

**Cause:** `shouldDeferSelfApprovalForCurrentTarget()` suppresses every deferred child `review` `SHIP`, including a re-review after parent-dispatched self-approval requested changes. Then `reportTerminalToParent()` skips because the child marker is already `done` and the original ready report was already dispatched, so the parent is not resumed.

**Candidate solutions:** Carry explicit parent-finalization retry context through `agent-self-approve -> fix-pr -> review`, or re-notify the parent when a `done` deferred child receives another `SHIP` after fixes. Add regression coverage for `agent-self-approve REQUEST_CHANGES -> fix-pr success -> review SHIP`.

**Comments:** This is the only required branch change before another automated review.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Non-blocking cleanup/test coverage nits remain</summary>

**Cause:** `parseSubOrchestratorMarker()` still has a guard that is unreachable after normalization, and the delegate CLI test adds `finalize_policy: "defer"` without directly asserting the created issue body contains `finalize:defer`.

**Candidate solutions:** Remove the dead guard or make normalization strict, and add a direct `ghLog` assertion for the created child issue body when convenient.

**Comments:** These were treated as minor by the stale review and are not included in required automation action items.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR

The remaining blocker is a concrete orchestration retry bug and is safe for an automated fix-pr pass with focused regression coverage.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Fix deferred child finalization after `agent-self-approve` returns `REQUEST_CHANGES` so the later `fix-pr -> review -> SHIP` path either retries parent finalization or dispatches self-approval again, with regression coverage.
